intended_object: The underlying affine K-scheme of the upper-unitriangular (unipotent upper-triangular) group scheme U_n over Spec K: Spec of the coordinate ring K[x_ij, 1/det]/(x_ij for j<i, x_ii − 1), seen as a scheme over Spec K. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation, and its use as the carrier of `unitriangularGroupScheme`.
explanation:
The definition is the affine scheme Spec(A) over Spec K, where A is the quotient of the GL_n coordinate ring K[x_ij][1/det] by the ideal generated by x_ij for j < i and x_ii − 1. A K-algebra map from A to R is the same as an invertible matrix over R that is upper triangular with ones on the diagonal. So this is exactly the standard coordinate ring of U_n. The library proves this: it constructs a natural group isomorphism, for every commutative K-algebra R, between the R-points of this scheme and the upper-unitriangular subgroup of GL_n(R) (`unitriangularGroupPointsIso`). Since x_ii = 1 forces det = 1, localizing at det makes no difference.

The definition is stated for any commutative base ring K and any finite linearly ordered index type n. The order is needed to say what "upper triangular" means, and finiteness is needed for the determinant. This is the natural generality. Mathlib has no unitriangular group scheme and no Hopf-algebra presentation of it, so there is no counterpart.

The object is the underlying scheme of the group scheme rather than the group scheme itself, but it is still a genuine mathematical object: U_n as a K-scheme.
